handoff.goals: Install the PostHog SDK using the project’s package manager and ensure the dependency is declared for later integration steps.
handoff.did: Inspected `package.json`, detected pnpm via the wizard tool, and found neither an existing PostHog dependency nor Next.js route handlers that send server-side events. Attempted `pnpm add posthog-js`; pnpm could not proceed because the existing `node_modules` is linked to `C:\Users\lemon\AppData\Local\pnpm\store\v10` while this pnpm invocation expects `C:\Users\lemon\.pnpm\store\v10`. Per the environment-failure fallback, added `posthog-js` at the known-good declaration `^1.407.2` to `package.json`. This makes the browser SDK importable as `posthog-js` once dependencies are installed; no server SDK was added because no server-side PostHog event code exists.
handoff.forNextAgent: Use `posthog-js` for the client integration. The lockfile and node_modules were not updated because pnpm was blocked by the pre-existing store-location mismatch. Resolve the pnpm store/reinstall dependencies in the user environment before build verification. No PostHog configuration was written in this task.
handoff.evidence: `detect_package_manager` reported pnpm and `pnpm add posthog-js` was attempted once. The command failed with `ERR_PNPM_UNEXPECTED_STORE`, explicitly identifying an existing node_modules store mismatch. The targeted manifest edit succeeded.
handoff.assumptions: The absence of Next.js App Router route files and PostHog capture references means only the client SDK is needed at this installation step.
handoff.conflict: `pnpm add posthog-js` could not update the lockfile because the project’s existing node_modules uses a different pnpm store location.

handoff.goals: Initialize PostHog once for the Next.js App Router client, configure its public environment variables, and document those variables for developers.
handoff.did: Created `src/app/PostHogClient.tsx`, a browser-only client component that imports the singleton `posthog-js` SDK and calls `posthog.init()` once when both `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` are present. It uses the configured host as `api_host`, enables exception capture, retains default capture behavior, and emits the prescribed development error if either configuration variable is absent; production remains a no-op. Mounted `<PostHogClient />` once in `src/app/layout.tsx`, so later client call sites must reach this same configured SDK via `import posthog from "posthog-js"`. Set the real public PostHog token and EU host in `.env.local` through `set_env_values`. Added placeholder documentation for both keys to `.env.example`. No CSP was detected, so no CSP directives (`script-src`, `connect-src`, or `worker-src`) were changed.
handoff.forNextAgent: The app is on Next.js 15.2, below the 15.3 instrumentation-client threshold, so the root-mounted client component is intentional. Import the default `posthog` singleton from `posthog-js` in client components; do not construct or initialize another client. No server-side PostHog client was added in this initialization task.
handoff.evidence: `check_env_keys` reported both `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` as present in `.env.local`; final file reads confirmed the guarded initializer and `.env.example` documentation. `package.json` also contains `posthog-js` (^1.407.2). Per task instructions, no build, lint, typecheck, or tests were run.
handoff.assumptions: The project does not ship a Content-Security-Policy: repository search found no application CSP configuration. The actual production deployment must supply the same two `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_*` variables.

handoff.goals: Wire PostHog user identification so browser events and exception capture are associated with the app's stable authenticated user ID, and reset that identity on logout.
handoff.did: Updated `convex/users.ts` so the existing authenticated `users.me` query deliberately exposes the immutable Convex `users` document ID alongside the existing name/email profile fields. Updated `src/app/ConvexClientProvider.tsx` with a root-mounted client identity synchronizer: after Convex resolves an authenticated user (including after login/signup and on page refresh), it calls `posthog.identify()` using that document ID as the distinct ID and sends optional email/name only as person properties. It first confirms the shared PostHog client was initialized. Updated `src/app/PostHogClient.tsx` to expose that initialization state for guarded downstream SDK calls. Updated the three explicit sign-out boundaries in `src/app/_components/Dashboard.tsx`, `src/app/_components/CourseShell.tsx`, and `src/app/_components/SettingsPage.tsx` to call guarded `posthog.reset()` before their existing Convex sign-out flow. This ensures subsequent browser events and exception autocapture inherit the persisted identified identity until logout.
handoff.forNextAgent: Client-side PostHog is initialized once by the root-mounted `PostHogClient`; client event/error callsites should import the singleton from `posthog-js` and do not need to identify per event. The root `PostHogIdentity` component identifies authenticated users from `api.users.me`; its ID is the stable Convex document ID, while email/name must remain person properties and never be included in capture event properties. All current `signOut()` callsites reset PostHog first. There is no server-side PostHog SDK or server event instrumentation in this project, so no tracing-header/server identity wiring was added.
handoff.evidence: Read the Convex auth callback and schema to confirm `getAuthUserId()` returns the stable `users` document ID and that email/name are optional profile fields. Reviewed the final identity component and all `signOut()` matches: the only three sign-out callsites each invoke guarded `posthog.reset()` before calling `signOut()`. Per task instruction, no build, lint, typecheck, or tests were run.
handoff.assumptions: The root layout continues to render `PostHogClient` before `ConvexClientProvider`, as observed, so `PostHogIdentity` runs against the already configured singleton. Convex deployment/code generation will pick up the expanded `api.users.me` return shape in the normal project workflow.

handoff.goals: Ensure uncaught Next.js App Router errors reach PostHog through one global framework error boundary, without installing dependencies or running verification commands.
handoff.did: Created `src/app/global-error.tsx`, the App Router global client error boundary. It initializes the existing PostHog singleton and uses `posthog.captureException(error)` in an effect to send errors handled by the global boundary to PostHog Error Tracking. Updated `src/app/PostHogClient.tsx` to expose an idempotent `initializePostHog()` helper, preserving the existing environment-variable guard, `capture_exceptions: true` initialization, and development error behavior. The helper now returns whether initialization is available, so the global boundary does not attempt a capture when production configuration is absent. This feeds PostHog Error Tracking with unhandled application failures via exception events.
handoff.forNextAgent: The error boundary is intentionally `src/app/global-error.tsx` because this is a Next.js App Router project. It imports the default `posthog-js` singleton and reuses the existing initializer rather than constructing a second client. No manual component- or route-level exception capture was added. The existing dependency installation remains subject to the prior pnpm store mismatch noted by the install task.
handoff.evidence: Final file reads confirm `global-error.tsx` invokes `posthog.captureException(error)` only after `initializePostHog()` succeeds, and `PostHogClient.tsx` initializes with the configured environment values, `capture_exceptions: true`, and idempotence. Per task constraints, no build, tests, lint, or package installation commands were run.
handoff.assumptions: Assumed the existing PostHog initialization from the prior task is the intended browser singleton and that App Router's `global-error.tsx` is the required framework-level boundary. The later build/review task should verify compilation.

handoff.goals: Select and instrument meaningful product events in the Next.js App Router app, preserving the existing PostHog identity model and documenting the resulting event contract.
handoff.did: Created `.posthog-wizard-cache/.posthog-events.json` with eight core events spanning authentication, access-code enrollment, voucher redemption, payment initiation, quiz responses, and lesson completion. In `src/app/_components/SignIn.tsx`, added guarded personless captures for password authentication submission and Google authentication start; properties only describe authentication flow and checkout intent. In `src/app/_components/JoinPanel.tsx`, added a guarded personless capture before access-code authentication; no access code or entered name is sent. In `src/app/_components/RedeemPanel.tsx`, captured successful voucher redemption after the authenticated mutation succeeds. In `src/app/_components/CheckoutPage.tsx`, captured successful card checkout creation immediately before redirect and successful EFT intent creation. In `src/app/_components/ArtifactView.tsx`, captured quiz answers with only the boolean correctness outcome and centralized lesson completion capture for advancing, finishing, and read-only next-lesson paths. All authenticated captures use the existing root PostHog identity; every capture is guarded by `isPostHogInitialized()` so missing optional configuration remains non-breaking.
handoff.forNextAgent: No build, lint, typecheck, or tests were run, per task instructions. The event manifest is the source of truth for the eight new events. Authentication submission and access-code join events correctly remain personless because identity does not exist at those action points; successful redemption, checkout, quiz, and completion captures inherit the root Convex-backed PostHog identity. No PII, entered credentials, access/voucher codes, course text, names, or emails are included in capture properties.
handoff.evidence: Final reads confirmed all eight planned events in the manifest and a targeted source search found matching guarded `posthog.capture()` calls in each listed component. The reviewed properties are limited to `flow`, `checkout_intent`, `correct`, and `completion_action`; no PII is captured.
handoff.assumptions: The root-mounted `PostHogClient` initializes before user actions occur and the existing `PostHogIdentity` synchronizer has identified authenticated Convex users, as established in the prior handoff.

handoff.goals: Install the declared PostHog SDK, verify the project-defined build/typecheck/lint checks, and strictly review the upstream integration changeset across minimality, unrelated changes, codebase patterns, and framework example shape.
handoff.did: Attempted the required single `pnpm install`; pnpm stopped at an interactive prompt asking to remove and reinstall the existing modules directory, so dependency provisioning did not complete. Reviewed every upstream changeset file (using the env-key tool for `.env` state), the changed query's callers, the framework reference, and neighboring component/config patterns. Made 6 review fixes: (1, Minimal/framework correctness) changed `src/app/PostHogClient.tsx` to initialize the external SDK in `useEffect` rather than during React render; (1, Codebase patterns) added both optional PostHog public variables to the existing `env.js` createEnv client schema/runtime map and consumed that typed config from the initializer; (4, Codebase patterns) normalized the new `posthog-js` import placement in `src/app/ConvexClientProvider.tsx`, `src/app/_components/Dashboard.tsx`, `src/app/_components/CourseShell.tsx`, and `src/app/_components/SettingsPage.tsx`. No event names, event properties, capture timing/locations, identity values, or logout behavior changed. Review dimensions: Minimal passes after the render-side-effect fix; Unrelated passes; Codebase patterns pass after config/import fixes; Example shapes pass for the Next.js 15.2 root-mounted singleton initializer, identity synchronization, guarded captures/resets, and global exception boundary.
handoff.forNextAgent: The code integration is in place, but `posthog-js` is still not installed in `node_modules` and absent from the lockfile. In an interactive terminal, run `pnpm install`, approve pnpm's clean reinstall prompt (or reconcile the existing pnpm store linkage), then rerun `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build`. There is no lint script. The environment keys are present in `.env.local`; production deployment must set the same public variables.
handoff.evidence: `check_env_keys` reported both `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_PROJECT_TOKEN` and `NEXT_PUBLIC_POSTHOG_HOST` present in `.env.local`. `pnpm typecheck` ran and its only diagnostics were TS2307 module-resolution failures for uninstalled `posthog-js` imports. `pnpm build` reached Next.js compilation and failed only with webpack `Module not found: Can't resolve 'posthog-js'`. `package.json` declares `posthog-js` as `^1.407.2`. No lint script is defined, and tests were not run.
handoff.assumptions: Because pnpm did not complete dependency provisioning, compilation beyond resolving `posthog-js` could not be observed. The reviewed source and framework patterns indicate no other integration-specific issue, but a successful install is required to prove that.
handoff.conflict: `pnpm install` stopped at an interactive clean-reinstall prompt, leaving `posthog-js` uninstalled; consequently `pnpm typecheck` and `pnpm build` fail only on resolving that declared module.

handoff.forNextAgent: Dashboard URL: https://eu.posthog.com/project/264778/dashboard/931180. It has five attached insight tiles and will populate as production events arrive; no repository files were changed in this task.

handoff.reportSection:
## Starter analytics dashboard

Created [Analytics basics (wizard)](https://eu.posthog.com/project/264778/dashboard/931180) with five event-contract-based views: authentication starts, checkout starts by payment method, quiz-to-lesson activation funnel, daily lesson completions, and quiz answer accuracy. The insights are attached to the dashboard and will populate as events arrive.
